title: Ar-Rafi', the Exalter
hook: the Exalter, who raises the humble
tomorrow: unveiling night. who's missing from the thank-you list?

segments.voice: Yesterday, al-Khafid: the Abaser, and Iblis lowered for saying I am better than him. He lowers. Now the other side of the same pair.
screen: `HE LOWERS.` → `THE OTHER SIDE OF THE PAIR.`

segments.voice: A shout-out in someone else's post can carry a person for a week. Yesterday's question: Amira gets one sentence in the caption, so who does she lift? She picks Luis, the barista who came in early to prime the wall and never asked to be in a picture. One question for today, then: who gets raised, and by whom?
screen: `ONE SHOUT-OUT, A WHOLE WEEK.` → `SHE PICKS LUIS.` → `WHO GETS RAISED?`

segments.voice: Islam's answer is a name: ar-Rafi', the Exalter, who raises the humble. In the traditional list it stands right beside yesterday's al-Khafid. In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet, peace be upon him, says, in paraphrase: charity never shrinks wealth, forgiving only adds to a person's honor, and no one humbles themselves for Allah's sake except that Allah raises them. And the Qur'an names who goes up, in Pickthall's words: "Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks." Now a neighbor who says it in her own words. In the Hebrew Bible, Hannah has prayed for a child, and when her son is born she sings. In her song, in the book of Samuel, the Lord makes poor and makes rich, brings low and lifts up, and raises the poor out of the dust to sit among princes. What the two share: the One who lowers the proud is the same One who lifts the low, and people don't hand out the real raising, God does. And an honest difference: Hannah sings about God's acts, as thanks for a son. In Islam, the Exalter is also a name, one of the names a believer calls on directly, beside its partner, the Abaser. Two ways of saying it, and one thing for a friend tonight: in both, the lifting starts at ground level, from the dust.
screen: `AR-RAFI': HE RAISES THE HUMBLE.` · `HUMBLE YOURSELF, AND BE RAISED.` · `HANNAH: OUT OF THE DUST.` · `SHARED, AND HONESTLY DIFFERENT.` · then, large: `HE RAISES.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person whose work usually goes unseen: a cook, a janitor, a coworker who does the boring part well. Write them a short message, just what they did and that it mattered, and use the sit to get the words right. Sending it is up to you.
screen: `ONE UNSEEN PERSON.` · `WHAT THEY DID. THAT IT MATTERED.`

segments.voice: Ar-Rafi': the Exalter, who raises the humble, from the dust and to high ranks. The partner of al-Khafid.
Hold this one: he raises, and the humble are the ones he lifts. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims learn al-Khafid and ar-Rafi' as a pair, and the hadith that humbling yourself for Allah's sake brings raising is taught alongside them.
